request.summary: Create a full-bleed video program that proves reliable file, folder, JSON playlist, HLS, caption, recovery, telemetry, and remote-control behavior without adding video runtime to unrelated custom apps.
request.audience: Visitors and employees watching unattended media programs, plus near-view operators using touch or external controls.
request.primaryGoal: Keep the active video visually dominant while making program identity, source order, current progress, and failure recovery unambiguous.

assumptions: Wallboard File System files and folders are resolved and cached through the SDK before playback.
The packaged fictional Lumen videos make the app immediately testable and act as the offline preview fallback.
hls.js 0.7.9 is pinned from the proven legacy renderer and exists only inside apps opting into the video capability.
Custom apps can emit playback sensor events but cannot call the platform native player, synchronized playback, audio ducking, or proof-of-display APIs through the current SDK.

surfaceStrategy.rationale: Full-screen programs and embedded playlist zones both need deliberate full-bleed playback and bounded chrome.

surfaces.purpose: Full-bleed landscape program with playlist rail and progress strip.
Wide playlist strip that removes secondary chrome before reducing media area.
Portrait program with horizontal source selector above the bottom status rail.
Square playlist tile that preserves active media and a bounded horizontal source selector.
Compact media tile retaining identity and progress without playlist clutter.

ownership.rationale: Operators choose one File System video, an ordered folder, or a structured playlist without code changes.
Each placement explicitly owns sound, fit, sequence, caption, and recovery behavior.
Preset-safe program chrome can be hidden completely or branded through a complete Custom palette.
Playback state is local to the placed app and resets on remount.
Control contents and automations operate the player without simulated pointer input.
Compatibility and lifecycle safety remain code-owned invariants.

views.purpose: Render the active video full bleed with optional program chrome.
Expose ordered playlist identity and direct source selection.

inputs.action: Select videos and use optional playback controls.
Use the same bounded controls on kiosk and touch displays.
Play, pause, seek, select, navigate, reload, mute, or set volume remotely.

session.expectation: Playback remains placement-local until remount, source update, completion policy, or explicit command.

outputs.expectation: Emit source, start, pause, quarter-progress, completion, and terminal failure interactions.
outputs.failure: Playback remains authoritative if telemetry is unavailable.

rendering.rationale: Video preserves its selected contain, cover, or fill behavior while program chrome reflows by assigned ratio.

motion.rationale: The video is the motion; decorative app transitions would compete with it.

media.fallback: Use the packaged fictional program and show a bounded source notice after a configured source error.
media.rationale: Production media is resolved through File System or explicit playlist settings and cached by Wallboard.

media.fallback: Show the designed no-source state if packaged fixtures are removed.
media.rationale: Small synthetic videos make local preview, visual QA, and an upload smoke test deterministic.

branding.provenance: The Lumen identity and synthetic videos are fictional and generated for this example.
branding.fallback: Use the coordinated Dark preset and fictional Lumen identity when no customer reference exists.

dynamicText.fallback: Ellipsize arbitrary filenames after preserving sequence and active state.
dynamicText.rationale: Media and progress geometry must not change for pathological filenames.

dynamicText.fallback: Ellipsize the venue label before reducing video area.

dynamicText.rationale: The active video remains the primary surface.

states.expectation: The synthetic two-item program autoplays muted and advances while chrome remains legible.
The wide-low surface preserves the full media viewport and reduces secondary chrome before primary status.
The light preset reflows playlist choices above the footer without covering primary media.
The square surface keeps playback dominant and the source selector bounded.
Secondary playlist chrome disappears before media or primary status becomes unreadable.
Long venue, program, and source labels remain bounded without changing playback geometry.
The custom palette changes the authored chrome while preserving readable text and media contrast.
A failed source retries a bounded number of times, emits failure telemetry, and advances or shows a designed fallback.

behaviors.expectation: The packaged WebM enters playing state and advances its progress through the real browser media element.
Completion and next/previous commands select exact playlist items without an empty frame.
Play, pause, seek, select, navigation, mute, and volume commands operate the active player.
Configured remote media, posters, and captions pass through the SDK cache path before rendering.
Failed media retries only the configured count and advances when policy permits.
Destroy pauses media, destroys HLS, removes source state, and clears retry timers.

visualDirection.summary: A cinematic program ident where video occupies the complete canvas and the UI behaves like quiet broadcast metadata rather than a dashboard.
references: Proven legacy Wallboard video and video-gallery playback behavior
signatureChoices: A compact numbered program ledger floats over the moving image.
A low broadcast progress rail carries current identity without framing the video in a card.
avoid: Bundling video or HLS code into non-video apps

visualReview.intent: A production media channel where the moving image remains primary and every overlay reads as deliberate broadcast chrome.
focus: Verify active video fills or letterboxes exactly according to the configured fit mode at every ratio.
Verify playlist, captions, program identity, and progress never cover essential center-frame content or overlap each other.
Verify long file and program names truncate cleanly without shrinking below room-readable floors.
Verify Dark, Light, and Custom palettes update every app-owned chrome color while leaving the video unchanged.
